item.title: Women should enter Parliament based on service, not gender - Adi Finau
item.description: Women should not seek a place in Parliament simply because they are women, but because they have built a record of service and have something meaningful to contribute. This has been highlighted by Soqosoqo Vakamarama iTaukei president Adi Finau Tabakaucoro while speaking to fijivillage News on women's participation in leadership and decision-making spaces.
item.content:encoded:
Women should not seek a place in Parliament simply because they are women, but because they have built a record of service and have something meaningful to contribute.

This has been highlighted by Soqosoqo Vakamarama iTaukei president Adi Finau Tabakaucoro while speaking to fijivillage News on women's participation in leadership and decision-making spaces.

Adi Finau says political representation must be backed by commitment, experience and a proven connection with communities.

Insert: Adi Finau - Service to the community July 06

She pointed to Minister for Environment Lynda Tabuya as an example of someone who has built recognition through community service .

While representation is important, she says more attention is needed on development issues that directly affect people's daily lives, including access to water, sanitation, healthcare and economic opportunities.

She says communities are often focusing heavily on discussions around rights, democracy and parliamentary representation, while basic needs and livelihood opportunities required greater attention.

Adi Finau says addressing these issues is a key focus of the Soqosoqo Vakamarama iTaukei's Strategic Development Plan 2025–2030, which aims to strengthen the organisation and empower women across Fiji.

The organisation has membership across all 14 provinces, 159 communities and 1,192 villages, and operates as a charitable trust.

She says a major focus of the plan is improving economic empowerment so women and communities could become more self-sufficient.

On domestic violence, Adi Finau says addressing the issue required a stronger focus on enforcement, adding that violence against women should be treated as a criminal matter.

S he acknowledged existing Government social protection programmes but says organisations such as Soqosoqo Vakamarama did not have the resources to replace government services.

Adi Finau says empowering women requires more than awareness alone, with greater emphasis needed on creating opportunities for communities to improve their livelihoods.

item.title: Claims sugar industry will collapse are nonsense - Kamikamica
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica has assured sugarcane farmers in Seaqaqa that Fiji's sugar industry will not collapse, following concerns raised during a public consultation. item.content:encoded:
Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica has assured sugarcane farmers in Seaqaqa that Fiji's sugar industry will not collapse, following concerns raised during a public consultation.

Responding to a farmer's concern that growers had heard claims the sugar industry was collapsing, Kamikamica described those claims as nonsense and stressed that if the sugar industry was collapsing, Government leaders, including Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka, would not be travelling to meet farmers and discuss ways to revive the sector.

Kamikamica says the presence of Government ministers, the Leader of the Opposition and representatives from other political parties showed that the sugar industry is a national issue rather than a political one.

INSERT: Kamikamica on sugar industry 6th Aug

Kamikamica acknowledged that there had been many previous attempts to address the industry's challenges, including numerous reports over the years, but stressed that the current Government is determined to ensure meaningful action is taken.

He says the Government believes there is a future for the sugar industry and is focused on finding practical solutions to strengthen it.
